results.content:
WASHINGTON, Sept 11 (Reuters) - U.S. consumer sentiment deteriorated in early September as rising gasoline prices ​and trade tensions stoked fears of ‌higher inflation over the next 12 months, a survey showed on Friday. [...] The survey's measure of consumer expectations for inflation over the ​next year jumped ​to ⁠4.6% from 4.0% last month. Twelve-month inflation expectations were at 3.4% in ​February before the U.S.-led war ​with ⁠Iran started. Consumers' expectations for inflation over the next five years edged up 3.4% from ⁠3.3% ​in August. They are ​higher than their 2024 range of 2.8% to 3.2%.

Reporting ​By Lucia Mutikani; Editing by Chizu Nomiyama

results.title: State of the US consumer: August 2026 - Deloitte

results.content:
Consumer sentiment plunged in September amid heightened inflation fears, hitting its second lowest level on record on the University of Michigan's monthly survey released Friday.

The survey's headline index hit a level of 47.8, down 7.5% from the August reading and off 13.2% from a year ago. This was the second lowest reading on record for data going back to 1952 — the bottom coming in May as rising prices also jolted the outlook.
